K and clottingK = Koagulation (German for clotting)

18. Mixed practice with worked answers

Structures for the worked questions

Structures for the worked questions

Q3: Gly–Ala–Val–Gly (stereogenic α-carbons: Ala and Val)
Q4 and Q17: Gly–Gly–Gly, C₆H₁₁N₃O₄ (two peptide bonds: biuret positive)Δ
Q5: H₂N–(CH₂)₃–COOHΔ, −H₂Oγ-butyrolactam: five-membered ring (N, 3 CH₂, C=O)
Q6: D-fructoseNaBH₄ or H₂/NiD-glucitol (sorbitol)+D-mannitol
Q7: D-galactose (RLLR)mirror image →L-galactose (LRRL)
D-glucoseBr₂/H₂O; Fe³⁺, H₂O₂Ruff degradation, −CO₂D-arabinosesame product(C-2 becomes the new CHO)D-mannose
Q9: 2,3-di-O-methylglucose (C4, C6 were unavailable: branch point residue)
Q11: trehalose (α,α-1,1′): non-reducing; only glucose on hydrolysis
Q12: 5′-AGTCC-3′ pairs with 3′-TCAGG-5′; reverse complement 5′-GGACT-3′
Q19: nucleoside (deoxyadenosine) = base + sugar+ phosphate →nucleotide (dAMP)
Q20: pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B₆ coenzyme)

1. pKₐ values of a triprotic amino acid are 2.2, 4.3 and 9.7. Its fully protonated form has charge +1. Find pI.

The charge sequence is +1, 0, −1, −2. The neutral state lies between 2.2 and 4.3. pI ≈ 3.25.

2. How many linear tripeptides can be formed from Ala, Gly and Ser if repetition is allowed?

Three independently chosen positions give 3³ = 27 sequences.

3. How many α-carbons in Gly–Ala–Val–Gly are stereogenic?

Two. Glycine has two hydrogens at Cα. Ala and Val each have four different groups at Cα.

4. What is the formula of Gly–Gly–Gly?

Subtract 2H₂O from three C₂H₅NO₂ units to obtain C₆H₁₁N₃O₄.

5. An amino acid has the structure H₂N–(CH₂)₃–COOH. What is the expected lactam ring size?

Five atoms. Count the nitrogen, three methylene carbons and carbonyl carbon.

6. Which sugar gives mannitol and glucitol on reduction?

D-Fructose. The planar C2 ketone becomes a new stereocentre.

7. An aldohexose has OH positions RLLR in its Fischer projection. Identify it and give its enantiomeric pattern.

D-Galactose. The L-galactose pattern is LRRL.

8. Why do glucose and mannose give the same Ruff product?

Their difference lies at C2, which becomes the new planar aldehyde carbon. Both give D-arabinose.

9. A glucan residue produces 2,3-di-O-methylglucose in methylation analysis. Which nonanomeric positions are linked?

C4 and C6 were unavailable for methylation. In a typical α-glucan this marks a branch residue.

10. A sample gives a deep blue iodine test. What should happen after complete hydrolysis to glucose?

The colour disappears as the starch helix is destroyed. Glucose gives a positive reducing test.

11. A disaccharide yields only glucose on hydrolysis and is nonreducing before hydrolysis. Which entry in the disaccharide table fits?

Trehalose. Its link joins the two anomeric carbons.

12. Write the reverse complement of 5′-AGTCC-3′.

3′-TCAGG-5′ is the aligned complement. Read it from its 5′ end to give 5′-GGACT-3′.

13. A DNA duplex contains 240 bp and 600 base-pair H bonds. Find the number of A–T pairs.

G–C pairs = 600 − 2(240) = 120. The remaining 120 pairs are A–T.

14. How many internucleotide phosphodiester links occur in a circular DNA duplex with 100 bp and two covalently closed strands?

Each strand has 100 links because it has no free ends. There are 200 links in total.

15. An enzyme reaches 75% of Vmax at 9 mM substrate. Estimate Kₘ.

From 0.75 = 9/(Kₘ + 9), Kₘ = 3 mM.

16. An inhibitor increases apparent Kₘ threefold while leaving Vmax unchanged. Which model fits?

Competitive inhibition. A higher substrate concentration reaches the same fraction of Vmax.

17. What is the shortest usual peptide chain that gives the Biuret reaction?

A tripeptide. It has two backbone peptide linkages.

18. One mole of an acyclic glucose oligomer gives six moles of glucose on complete hydrolysis. Find its formula.

Six glucose units lose five waters when assembled, giving C₃₆H₆₂O₃₁.

19. What distinguishes a nucleotide from a nucleoside?

A nucleotide has at least one phosphate group in addition to its base and sugar.

20. Which vitamin supplies the coenzyme involved in many aminotransferase reactions?

Vitamin B₆ supplies pyridoxal phosphate, which temporarily accepts the amino group during transamination.

Worked applications on amino acids, proteins and nucleic acids

  1. Assign pI from 2.2, 4.3 and 9.7 for an amino acid with an acidic side chain. The charge sequence is +1 → 0 → −1 → −2. The two values around charge zero give pI = 3.25.
  2. Count the water loss for six residues in a linear peptide and in a head-to-tail cyclic peptide. The formal losses are five and six H₂O, respectively.
  3. Assign a level of structure to a disulfide between two insulin chains. It is a covalent link between subunits and contributes to their assembly. A disulfide between two sites of one chain instead contributes to the fold of that chain.
  4. For a 120 bp linear DNA duplex containing 32 G–C pairs, count interbase H bonds and backbone phosphodiesters. There are 2(88) + 3(32) = 272 H bonds and 2(119) = 238 phosphodiesters.
  5. Which species contains both a phosphoester and phosphoanhydrides, adenosine, AMP or ATP? ATP. Its ribose is joined to the first phosphate by an ester and its adjacent phosphate groups are connected through P–O–P.
  6. A violet Hopkins–Cole result is obtained with a peptide. What does it identify? A tryptophan side-chain indole under the conditions of that test. It gives no residue order.

Assignment questions with structures and answers

141 questions covering every question type in the chapter, grouped by topic. Similar questions are merged into one, so a single item may have several parts. Attempt each one, then open Answer and solution.

Carbohydrates: structure, stereochemistry, reducing sugars, osazones and oxidation

Q1One or more options correct

Which of the following are disaccharides and also reducing sugars?

  1. lactose
  2. sucrose
  3. cellulose (repeating cellobiose unit)
  4. maltose
Answer and solution

Answer: (1) and (4)

Lactose (galactose + glucose) and maltose (glucose + glucose) keep one free hemiacetal group. Sucrose is a non-reducing disaccharide and cellulose is a polysaccharide.

Q2One or more options correct

Carbohydrates may be:

  1. sugars
  2. starch
  3. polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones
  4. compounds that give polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones on hydrolysis
Answer and solution

Answer: (1), (2), (3) and (4)

All four describe carbohydrates: sugars, polysaccharides such as starch, the monosaccharides themselves, and anything that hydrolyses to them.

Q3Single correct option

Paragraph. A carbohydrate with n asymmetric carbons has 2ⁿ optical isomers. (a) How many optical isomers does glucose have? (b) Fructose is a: (c) The first (smallest) ketose is a:

  1. (a) 8, 16, 32 or 4
  2. (b) aldotriose, ketohexose, aldohexose or ketotriose
  3. (c) ketotriose, ketotetrose, ketopentose or ketohexose
Answer and solution

Answer: (a) 16; (b) ketohexose; (c) ketotriose

Glucose has 4 stereocentres, so 2⁴ = 16. Fructose is a six-carbon ketose. The simplest ketose is dihydroxyacetone, a ketotriose.

Q4One or more options correct

Select the correct statements about anomers:

α-D-glucopyranoseβ-D-glucopyranose
  1. Anomers differ in configuration at C-1, the anomeric carbon
  2. α-D-Glucopyranose and β-D-glucopyranose are anomers
  3. Both anomers of D-glucopyranose can be crystallised and purified
  4. When pure α-D-glucopyranose is dissolved in water its optical rotation changes slowly
Answer and solution

Answer: (1), (2), (3) and (4)

Anomers are cyclic epimers at C-1. Each can be isolated, and each shows mutarotation until the equilibrium mixture is reached.

Q5One or more options correct

Which pairs are correctly matched?

  1. α-D-(+)-glucose and β-D-(+)-glucose: C-2 epimers
  2. Glucose and fructose: C-3 epimers
  3. Glucose: mutarotation
  4. Sucrose: glucose + fructose on hydrolysis
Answer and solution

Answer: (3) and (4)

The α and β forms are anomers (C-1), not C-2 epimers. Glucose and fructose are functional (aldose/ketose) isomers, not epimers.

Q6One or more options correct

Which statements are true?

  1. Oxidation of glucose with bromine water gives glutamic acid
  2. The two six-membered cyclic hemiacetal forms of D-(+)-glucose are called anomers
  3. Hydrolysis of sucrose gives dextrorotatory glucose and laevorotatory fructose
  4. Monosaccharides cannot be hydrolysed to simpler polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones
Answer and solution

Answer: (2), (3) and (4)

Bromine water oxidises the CHO group of glucose to gluconic acid, not an amino acid.

Q7Single correct option

The Fischer projection of D-glucose is shown. Which structure is β-L-glucopyranose?

D-glucose
  1. (1)
  2. (2)
  3. (3)
  4. (4)
Answer and solution

Answer: (4)

L-Glucose is the mirror image of D-glucose at every stereocentre. β means the anomeric OH is on the same side as the CH₂OH of the ring (trans to the C-5 substituent as in β-D), so β-L is the mirror image of β-D-glucopyranose, structure (4).

Q8One or more options correct

In the Fischer projection of L-arabinose, the OH groups at C-2, C-3 and C-4 lie on the sides given below. Mark the INCORRECT options.

D-arabinose (for reference)
  1. (1)
  2. (2)
  3. (3)
  4. (4)
Answer and solution

Answer: (2), (3) and (4)

D-Arabinose is C2 left, C3 right, C4 right; its mirror image L-arabinose is right, left, left (option 1). The other three are not L-arabinose.

Q9Single correct option

Which of these aldoses give the same osazone? (I) D-glucose (II) D-gulose (III) D-mannose (IV) D-galactose

D-riboseD-arabinoseD-xyloseD-lyxose
D-alloseD-altroseD-glucoseD-mannoseD-guloseD-idoseD-galactoseD-talose
  1. I, III
  2. I, III, IV
  3. I, II
  4. III, IV
Answer and solution

Answer: (1)

Osazone formation destroys C1 and C2 stereochemistry; sugars identical at C3–C5 give the same osazone. Glucose and mannose (C-2 epimers) match; gulose and galactose differ at C3–C5.

Q10Single correct option

D-Lyxose is treated with NaCN/HCl, then H₂/Pd–BaSO₄, then H₃O⁺ (Kiliani–Fischer). The final aldose can be:

D-lyxoseNaCNHClA′H₂/Pd–BaSO₄B′H₃O⁺C′ = ?
  1. D-galactose
  2. D-talose
  3. both (1) and (2)
  4. none of these
Answer and solution

Answer: (3)

Cyanide adds to the carbonyl, creating a new C-2 centre in either configuration. Reduction and hydrolysis give a pair of C-2 epimers, D-galactose and D-talose.

Q11Single correct option

Which Fischer description corresponds to L-gulose? (D-gulose has OH at C2 right, C3 right, C4 left, C5 right.)

  1. (1)
  2. (2)
  3. (3)
  4. (4)
Answer and solution

Answer: (2)

L-Gulose is the mirror image of D-gulose, so every OH is reversed.

Q12Single correct option

Paragraph. A (C₅H₁₀O₄) is oxidised by Br₂/H₂O to acid B (C₅H₁₀O₅). A forms a triacetate, is reduced by red P + HI to n-pentane, and with HIO₄ gives 1 mol HCHO and 1 mol HCOOH. (a) A is: (b) B is: (c) With PhNHNH₂, A gives:

A: 2-deoxypentose, C₅H₁₀O₄Br₂, H₂OB: 2-deoxypentonic acid  |PhNHNH₂phenylhydrazone only (no osazone)
Ared P + HIn-pentane |HIO₄HCHO + HCOOH + …
  1. (a) HOCH₂–CHOH–CHOH–CH₂–CHO, 2-deoxypentose
  2. (b) HOCH₂–CHOH–CHOH–CH₂–COOH, 2-deoxypentonic acid
  3. (c) the phenylhydrazone HOCH₂–CHOH–CHOH–CH₂–CH=N–NHPh (no osazone)
Answer and solution

Answer: A = 2-deoxypentose; B = 2-deoxypentonic acid; hydrazone only

C₅H₁₀O₄ is a pentose minus one O. n-Pentane shows a straight chain; three OH groups give a triacetate. HIO₄ cleaves the C3–C4 and C4–C5 diols (HCOOH from C4 and HCHO from C5). C2 is CH₂, so the second equivalent of PhNHNH₂ cannot form an osazone.

Q13One or more options correct

Paragraph. Two molecules of a pyranose (I) condense with loss of water to a disaccharide (II) with an α-1,4 link, and II polymerises to starch. (a) Compound I: (b) Compound II:

glucose (I)+glucose (I)−H₂Odisaccharide (II)polymerisationstarch (III)
  1. (a) has a hemiacetal structure
  2. (a) has an acetal structure
  3. (b) is an oligosaccharide
  4. (b) is a polysaccharide
Answer and solution

Answer: (1) and (3)

The free anomeric –OH of glucopyranose makes it a cyclic hemiacetal. A disaccharide is an oligosaccharide.

Q14One or more options correct

Glucose is treated with CH₃OH/dry HCl to give α- and β-methyl glucosides. Which statements are correct?

D-glucoseCH₃OHdry HClα-D-methylglucoside+β-D-methylglucoside
  1. Methyl glucosides do not react with Fehling’s or Tollens’ reagent
  2. The reaction passes through a carbocation (oxocarbenium ion)
  3. The two glucosides are enantiomers
  4. The non-reducing nature shows that no free –CHO group is available
Answer and solution

Answer: (1), (2) and (4)

The two products are anomers (diastereomers), not enantiomers. The acetal cannot open to the aldehyde, so it is non-reducing.

Q15One or more options correct

Which reactions of glucose can be explained only by its cyclic structure?

open-chain glucose (free CHO)⇌α-pyranose (hemiacetal)⇌β-pyranose (hemiacetal)
  1. It forms gluconic acid with ammoniacal AgNO₃ followed by acidification
  2. Its pentaacetate does not react with NH₂OH
  3. It does not respond to Schiff’s test
  4. It does not form the NaHSO₃ addition product
Answer and solution

Answer: (2), (3) and (4)

Oxidation to gluconic acid is an aldehyde reaction (open chain). Lack of oxime, Schiff and bisulphite reactions shows the CHO is masked as a hemiacetal.

Q16One or more options correct

Which statements are true for D-glucose?

D-glucose (Fischer)α-D-glucopyranoseopen chain (CHO)
  1. It gives Schiff’s reagent test
  2. It is the C-2 epimer of D-mannose
  3. Br₂/H₂O oxidises it to saccharic acid
  4. It shows mutarotation
Answer and solution

Answer: (2) and (4)

Glucose gives no Schiff test (hemiacetal), and bromine water gives gluconic acid; saccharic (glucaric) acid needs HNO₃.

Q17One or more options correct

D-Glucose on oxidation with HNO₃ gives glucaric acid with [α]D = +52.7°. Which sugars give the glucaric acid with [α]D = −52.7°?

D-glucoseHNO₃D-glucaric acid [α] = +52.7°
  1. D-glucose
  2. L-gulose
  3. L-glucose
  4. D-gulose
Answer and solution

Answer: (3) and (4)

The (−) acid is L-glucaric acid, formed from L-glucose and from D-gulose. D-Glucose and L-gulose both give the (+) acid.

Q18One or more options correct

The osazone of D-galactose cannot be obtained from:

given osazone
  1. D-glucose
  2. D-fructose
  3. D-mannose
  4. D-tagatose
Answer and solution

Answer: (1), (2) and (3)

Galactosazone differs from glucosazone at C-4. D-Tagatose and D-talose give the same osazone as galactose.

Q19One or more options correct

Which of these give an osazone identical (same melting point and crystal shape) to the osazone of D-glucose?

  1. D-mannose
  2. D-fructose
  3. D-glucose
  4. D-galactose
  5. D-allose
Answer and solution

Answer: (1), (2) and (3)

Osazone formation fixes only C-1 and C-2. Mannose, fructose and glucose have the same C3–C5 configuration; galactose differs at C-4 and allose at C-3.

Q20One or more options correct

Specific rotations: (+)-sucrose +66°, (+)-maltose +140°, L-(−)-glucose −52°, L-(+)-fructose +92°. For invert sugar the correct statements are:

D-fructose (−92°)+D-glucose (+52°)→ invert sugar
  1. It is made by acid-catalysed hydrolysis of maltose
  2. It is an equimolar mixture of D-(+)-glucose and D-(−)-fructose
  3. Its specific rotation is −20°
  4. Br₂ water oxidises it to saccharic acid as one of the products
Answer and solution

Answer: (2) and (3)

Invert sugar comes from sucrose. D-Glucose +52° and D-fructose −92° give (52 − 92)/2 = −20°. Bromine water gives gluconic acid, not saccharic acid.

Q21One or more options correct

Molisch’s test: which statements are correct?

  1. Starch does not respond because it is a polysaccharide
  2. Conc. H₂SO₄ converts carbohydrates to furfural or 5-hydroxymethylfurfural
  3. Furfural derivatives with 1-naphthol give a deep violet compound
  4. The violet ring forms at the junction of the two liquids
Answer and solution

Answer: (2), (3) and (4)

All classes of carbohydrates, including polysaccharides, respond; statement (1) is false.

Q22One or more options correct

Sucrose (X) hydrolyses to Y (glucose) + Z (fructose); lactose (P) hydrolyses to Y + R (galactose). Which pairs are distinguished by the test named?

sucrose (X)H₂O/H⁺glucose (Y)+fructose (Z)
lactose (P)H₂O/H⁺glucose (Y)+galactose (R)
  1. X and Y by Benedict’s test
  2. Y and Z by Seliwanoff’s test
  3. P and R by Barfoed’s test
  4. P and X by Tollens’ test
Answer and solution

Answer: (1), (2), (3) and (4)

Sucrose is non-reducing and glucose reducing; fructose (a ketose) gives Seliwanoff’s red but glucose does not; galactose (monosaccharide) responds to Barfoed’s quickly but lactose does not; lactose reduces Tollens’ reagent but sucrose does not.

Q23One or more options correct

Sugar X is sucrose (an α-glucoside of fructose, joined C1–C2) and sugar Y is cellobiose (glucose β-1,4-glucose). Select the correct statements.

sugar X (sucrose)sugar Y (cellobiose)
  1. X is reducing and Y is non-reducing
  2. X is non-reducing and Y is reducing
  3. The glycosidic linkages in X and Y are α and β respectively
  4. The glycosidic linkages in X and Y are β and α respectively
Answer and solution

Answer: (2) and (3)

Sucrose has no free anomeric OH; cellobiose has one. Sucrose is an α-glucoside and cellobiose a β-glucoside.

Q24Single correct option

Which disaccharide is a reducing sugar with an α-glycosidic linkage?

  1. (1) trehalose
  2. (2) cellobiose
  3. (3) maltose
  4. (4) sucrose
Answer and solution

Answer: (3)

Trehalose and sucrose are non-reducing (both anomeric carbons are engaged); cellobiose is β-linked.

Q25One or more options correct

Which statements are correct?

compound (1) maltoselactose (2)compound (3) sucrosecompound (4) cellobiose
  1. Maltose contains an α-1,4 glycosidic linkage
  2. Lactose is a non-reducing disaccharide
  3. Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar
  4. A disaccharide with a free hemiacetal OH, such as cellobiose, is a reducing sugar
Answer and solution

Answer: (1), (3) and (4)

Lactose has a free anomeric OH on its glucose unit and is reducing.

Q26One or more options correct

Select the INCORRECT statements about maltose:

maltose
  1. The linkage is α-C1–C4
  2. Maltose is a non-reducing sugar
  3. Maltose and sucrose give similar products on hydrolysis
  4. Maltose is a reducing sugar
Answer and solution

Answer: (2) and (3)

Maltose is reducing and gives two glucose units; sucrose gives glucose and fructose.

Q27One or more options correct

Select the correct statements about starch:

amylose unit: α-1,4 linked glucosesucrose (for comparison)
  1. It is a pure single compound
  2. It is a mixture of two polysaccharides of glucose, amylose and amylopectin
  3. All glucose units are joined by α-glycosidic links
  4. Amylose is an unbranched chain of α-1,4 linked glucose units
  5. Amylopectin is branched, with α-1,6 links at the branch points
  6. Its animal counterpart is glycogen
Answer and solution

Answer: (2), (3), (4), (5) and (6)

Starch is not a single compound. Amylose (water soluble) has α-1,4 links; amylopectin (insoluble) has α-1,4 chains with α-1,6 branches; animals store glycogen.

Q28One or more options correct

Which of these develops a blue colour with iodine?

  1. Glucose
  2. Amylose
  3. Starch
  4. Fructose
Answer and solution

Answer: (2) and (3)

Iodine fits inside the helix of amylose and starch to give the blue inclusion complex.

Q29Matching

Match the description with the carbohydrate. I: yields only glucose on hydrolysis; II: yields glucose and fructose; III: yields glucose and galactose; IV: reduces Fehling’s solution. Choices: P sucrose, Q lactose, R amylose, S mannose, T cellulose.

Answer and solution

Answer: I → R, T; II → P; III → Q; IV → Q, S

Amylose and cellulose are glucose polymers; sucrose gives glucose + fructose; lactose gives glucose + galactose; lactose and mannose are reducing.

Q30Matching

Match each carbohydrate with its hydrolysis product or property: A sucrose, B maltose, C cellulose, D lactose; P glucose + galactose, Q two units of α-D-glucose, R α-D-glucose + β-D-fructose, S β-D-glucose, T invert sugar.

Answer and solution

Answer: A → R, T; B → Q; C → S; D → P

Sucrose gives α-glucose and β-fructose (invert sugar); maltose gives two α-glucose; cellulose is built from β-glucose; lactose gives glucose + galactose.

Q31Matching

Match: A fructose, B zwitterion, C peptide linkage, D cane sugar and its hydrolysis. (1) protein, (2) inversion, (3) α-amino acid, (4) carbohydrate, (5) ketose.

Answer and solution

Answer: A → 4, 5; B → 1, 3; C → 1; D → 2, 4, 5

Fructose is a carbohydrate and a ketose. A zwitterion belongs to α-amino acids (and proteins). The peptide link is the protein bond. Sucrose hydrolysis is inversion and involves carbohydrates and a ketose (fructose).

Q32Numerical answer

A pyranose has specific rotation +150° for its α-form and +52° for its β-form. The equilibrium mixture of the anomers in solution rotates by +80°. What is the percentage of the α-form?

Answer and solution

Answer: 28.57

150x + 52(1 − x) = 80 gives x = 28/98 = 0.2857.

Q33Numerical answer

D-(+)-Glucose is oxidised with HNO₃ to P. How many stereoisomers are possible for P (including P itself)?

Answer and solution

Answer: 10

P is glucaric acid, a symmetric diacid with 4 stereocentres: 2³ + 2¹ = 10.

Q34Numerical answer

D-(+)-Glucose is oxidised with Br₂/H₂O to Q. How many stereoisomers are possible for Q (including Q itself)?

a = 2 (Asp, Glu), b = 3 (Lys, Arg, His), c = 4 (Phe, Tyr, Trp, His): 2 × 3/4 = 1.5.

Q97Numerical answer

Find the total number of chiral carbons in glycine, alanine, arginine and lysine together.

GlyAlaArgLys
Answer and solution

Answer: 3

Glycine has none; alanine, arginine and lysine have one each.

Q98Numerical answer

Which of proline, glutamine, serine and valine is an essential amino acid? Give the total number of hydrogen atoms in it.

(a) proline(b) glutamine(c) valine(d) serine
Answer and solution

Answer: 11

Valine (C₅H₁₁NO₂) has 11 H atoms.

Q99Numerical answer

At pH 5, with pKa(α-COOH, α-NH₃⁺, side chain): Arg 2.17, 9.04, 12.48; Ala 2.34, 9.69; Asp 2.09, 9.82, 3.86; Lys 2.18, 8.95, 10.79; Glu 2.19, 9.67, 4.25; Val 2.32, 9.62. X = number moving to the cathode; Y = number of non-essential ones moving to the anode. Find X/Y.

pI = ½(pKa of the two groups around the neutral form)
Answer and solution

Answer: 2

pI: Arg 10.76, Ala 6.02, Asp 2.98, Lys 9.87, Glu 3.22, Val 5.97. At pH 5, Arg, Ala, Lys and Val are cations (X = 4); Asp and Glu are anions and non-essential (Y = 2).

Q100Numerical answer

Among leucine, lysine, serine, cysteine, proline, threonine, arginine and histidine, X are essential. In the phosphodiester link of a dinucleotide, carbon Y of one sugar and carbon Z of the other are joined by the phosphate. Find X ÷ (Y + Z).

LeuLysSerCys
ProThrArgHis
Answer and solution

Answer: 0.625

X = 5 (Leu, Lys, Thr, Arg, His); the link is 3′–5′, so Y + Z = 8; 5/8 = 0.625.

Q101Numerical answer

How many of aspartic acid, serine, tyrosine, cysteine, phenylalanine, histidine, valine, arginine and alanine are basic amino acids?

AspSerTyrCysPhe
HisValArgAla

Histidine and arginine.

Q102Numerical answer

Valine has pKa(COOH) = 2.31 and pKa(NH₃⁺) = 9.69. Compute its pI.

valine: pKa 2.31 (COOH), 9.69 (NH₃⁺)
Answer and solution

Answer: 6.00

(2.31 + 9.69)/2 = 6.00.

Q103Numerical answer

Glutamic acid has pKa values 2.19 (α-COOH), 4.34 (side chain) and 9.73 (α-NH₃⁺). Find its isoelectric point.

glutamic acid: pKa 2.19 (α-COOH), 4.34 (side chain), 9.73 (NH₃⁺)
Answer and solution

Answer: 3.26 – 3.27

(2.19 + 4.34)/2 = 3.265.

Q104Numerical answer

The pKa values of the three ionisable groups of glutamic acid are 4.3 (side chain), 9.7 (NH₃⁺) and 2.2 (α-COOH). Find the isoelectric point.

glutamic acid: α-COOH 2.2 (z), side-chain COOH 4.3 (x), NH₃⁺ 9.7 (y)
Answer and solution

Answer: 3.25

(2.2 + 4.3)/2 = 3.25 (about 3).

Q105Numerical answer

X is lysine, Y is glycine and Z is aspartic acid. How many statements are correct? (a) X and Z are essential, Y is not; (b) X, Y, Z are basic, neutral and acidic; (c) with the same NaNO₂ + HCl all give the same amount of N₂; (d) at most 12 dipeptides form from X, Y, Z; (e) Y is optically inactive, X and Z active; (f) at pH 6–7, Z is cationic; (g) at pH 6–7, X is anionic.

XYZ
Answer and solution

Answer: 2

Correct: (b) and (e). Asp is non-essential; lysine gives twice as much N₂; the ordered pairs number 9, not 12; Asp is anionic and Lys cationic at pH 6–7.

Q106Numerical answer

An amino acid has three ionisable groups with pKa₁ = 2, pKa₂ = 4 and pKa₃ = 10 (the first two are –COOH groups). Find its isoelectric point.

acidic amino acid, pKa 2 (α-COOH), 4 (side-chain COOH), 10 (NH₃⁺)
Answer and solution

(2 + 4)/2 = 3.

Q107Numerical answer

lysine form shown

The free α-NH₂ and the carboxylate –COO⁻.

Q108Numerical answer

The three acidic groups P (side-chain COOH), Q (NH₃⁺) and R (α-COOH) of aspartic acid have pKa values 5, 10 and 3. Find the pI.

R = α-COOH (pKa 3), Q = NH₃⁺ (pKa 10), P = side-chain COOH (pKa 5)

(3 + 5)/2 = 4.

peptide: Ala–tBuGly–cyclopropylAla–Ala–Gly
Answer and solution

Only Ala and Gly are natural.

Q110Numerical answer

A peptide contains Gln, Cys, Ser, S-methylcysteine, 4-methylphenylalanine, Asp, cyclobutylglycine and Tyr. How many different natural amino acids result from complete hydrolysis?

peptide: Gln–Cys–Ser–S-Me-Cys–(4-Me)Phe–Asp–cyclobutylGly–Tyr

An α-amino acid (R = –CH₂COOH) has three acidic groups with pKa 2.5, 4.5 and 10. Find its isoelectric point.

cation (A), R = –CH₂COOH: pKa 2.5, 4.5, 10
Answer and solution

(2.5 + 4.5)/2 = 3.5.

Q114Numerical answer

A decapeptide (M = 796) on complete hydrolysis gives glycine (75), alanine and phenylalanine, and glycine is 47.0 % of the total mass of the hydrolysed products. What is the total number of alanine plus phenylalanine units?

a decapeptide has 9 –CO–NH– bonds; example fragment Gly–Ala–Phe
Answer and solution

Answer: 4

Products weigh 796 + 9(18) = 958; Gly = 450 g = 6 units; 10 − 6 = 4.

Q115Numerical answer

How many water molecules are needed for complete hydrolysis of a decapeptide chain?

Answer and solution

Answer: 9

A decapeptide has 9 peptide bonds. (Insulin, 51 residues, needs 50.)

Q116Numerical answer

For the same decapeptide (M = 796; glycine contributes 47.0 % of the products’ mass), how many glycine units are present?

Answer and solution

Answer: 6

0.47 × 958 ≈ 450 g, and 450/75 = 6.

Q117Numerical answer

For the peptide Val–Tyr–Asp–Thr–Gly–Ser, Z₁, Z₂ and Z₃ are the net charges at pH 2.0, 5.0 and 11.0. Find Z₁ + Z₂ + Z₃.

partial sequence of the active site of pepsin: Val–Tyr–Asp–Thr–Gly–Ser
Answer and solution

Answer: −3

pH 2: +1; pH 5: +1 − 1 (Asp) − 1 (C-term) = −1; pH 11: Asp −1, C-term −1, Tyr −1 = −3. Sum = −3.

Q118Numerical answer

How many peptide bonds are present in the sequence Val–Tyr–Asp–Thr–Gly–Ser?

partial sequence of the active site of pepsin: Val–Tyr–Asp–Thr–Gly–Ser
Answer and solution

Answer: 5

Six residues give five peptide bonds.

Q119Numerical answer

For Tyr–Asp–Lys, the absolute net charges at pH 2, 6 and 11 are |z₁|, |z₂| and |z₃|. Find |z₁| + |z₂| + |z₃|.

Tyr–Asp–Lys
Answer and solution

Answer: 5

pH 2: +2; pH 6: +1 + 1 − 1 − 1 = 0; pH 11: −3. Total 2 + 0 + 3 = 5.

Q120Numerical answer

How many are positively charged at pH 7?

H₃N⁺–CH₂–CO–NH–CH(R₁)–CO–NH–CH(R₂)–CO–NH–CH₂–COO⁻

IV (+1), VI (+2), VIII (+1) and IX (+2).

Q121Numerical answer

A tetrapeptide gives, on partial hydrolysis, the dipeptide Gly–Ala (or Ala–Gly) and two other amino acids; complete hydrolysis gives Phe, Gly and Ala only. How many tetrapeptide sequences are possible?

Gly–AlaAla–GlyPhe
Answer and solution

Answer: 6

Composition Gly, Ala, Phe, Phe: block (2 orders) among {block, Phe, Phe}: 3 × 2 = 6.

Q122Numerical answer

A tetrapeptide has –COOH on alanine and gives Gly, Val, Phe and Ala on complete hydrolysis. How many primary structures have the free –NH₂ on a chiral carbon?

tetrapeptide: C-terminal Ala; residues Gly, Val, Phe + Ala
Answer and solution

Answer: 4

Ala is last. The first residue must not be Gly: choose Val or Phe (2 ways), then 2 ways to order the rest = 4. (JEE Advanced 2013)

Q123Numerical answer

A tetrapeptide has –NH₂ on glycine and gives Gly, Val, Leu and Ala on hydrolysis. How many sequences have Val never carrying the free –COOH?

tetrapeptide: N-terminal Gly; Val, Leu, Ala
Answer and solution

Answer: 4

Gly is first; the other three can be ordered 3! = 6 ways; 2 have Val last: 6 − 2 = 4.

Q124Numerical answer

N-terminal Ala, second residue chiral
Answer and solution

Answer: 4

Residue 2 is Phe or Leu (2 ways); the remaining two can be ordered in 2 ways: 4.

Q125Numerical answer

2³ = 8.

Four residues give three linkages.

Q127Numerical answer

How many peptide linkages are in alanylglycylleucylalanylvaline?

alanylglycylleucylalanylvaline

A pentapeptide has 4 peptide bonds.

Q128Numerical answer

How many C=O groups are present in the tripeptide Asp–Glu–Lys?

Asp–Glu–Lys
Answer and solution

Two peptide C=O, two side-chain COOH (Asp, Glu) and the terminal COOH.

Q129Numerical answer

By the rule “two or more of –CO–NH–, –CO–NH₂, –CH₂–NH₂, –C(=NH)NH₂, –CS–NH₂”, how many of glycine, glycylalanine, a tripeptide and alanine give a positive biuret test?

glycineglycylalaninetripeptide (Gly–Gly–Gly)alanine

Glycylalanine and the tripeptide satisfy the rule; glycine and alanine have only one such group.

Q130Numerical answer

The sequence is Ala–Arg–Lys–Phe–Gly–His, so Gly is residue 5.

Nucleic acids and vitamins

Q131One or more options correct

Which of these is a deoxyribonucleotide?

  1. (1) dAMP
  2. (2) AMP
  3. (3) UMP
  4. (4) dCMP
Answer and solution

Answer: (1) and (4)

Deoxyribonucleotides contain 2-deoxyribose and the bases A, G, C or T. Uracil and ribose mark RNA nucleotides.

Q132One or more options correct

Select the correct statements: (a) If one DNA strand read 3′→5′ is ACTGTGAC, the complementary strand read 3′→5′ is GTCACAGT; (b) cytosine, thymine and uracil are purines; (c) a nucleic acid is a polynucleotide linked by phosphodiester bonds; (d) A–T has two and G–C three hydrogen bonds; (e) vitamin C is water soluble.

3′–A C T G T G A C–5′5′–T G A C A C T G–3′ (complement)
Answer and solution

Answer: (a), (c), (d) and (e)

Complementary pairing: A–T, C–G, so the antiparallel complement of 3′-ACTGTGAC-5′ is 5′-TGACACTG-3′, which read 3′→5′ is GTCACAGT. C, T and U are pyrimidines.

Q133Numerical answer

How many oxygen atoms are present in one molecule of β-D-2-deoxyribose?

β-D-2-deoxyribose
Answer and solution

Answer: 4

2-Deoxyribose is C₅H₁₀O₄.

Q134Numerical answer

How many oxygen atoms are present in a nucleotide formed from the base found only in RNA, ribose and phosphate?

uridine 5′-monophosphate (UMP): base uracil + ribose + phosphate
Answer and solution

UMP, C₉H₁₃N₂O₉P, has 9 O.

Q135Numerical answer

In E. coli DNA the ratio (A + T)/(G + C) is 0.93, and the sample contains 465 000 mol of adenine. The number of guanine units is x × 10ʸ. Find x + y.

A = T and G ≡ C; (A + T)/(G + C) = 0.93; A = T = 465 000
Answer and solution

Answer: 10

A = T = 465 000, A + T = 930 000, G + C = 1 000 000, G = 5 × 10⁵, so x = 5, y = 5 and x + y = 10.

Q136Numerical answer

uracil C₄H₄N₂O₂
Answer and solution

Answer: 25

Mass of N = 28 out of 112: 25 %.

Mixed and sequence problems

Q137Single correct option

Match the reaction with the observation. P: benzyl alcohol + 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene → ether; Q: PhNO₂ → Sn/HCl → NaNO₂/HCl (<5 °C) → 2-naphthol/OH⁻; R: n-glucose polymerises to starch (H⁺); S: amino acids polymerise to a protein. (1) Molisch test positive; (2) violet colour with neutral FeCl₃; (3) Lassaigne extract gives blue with FeSO₄ (N present); (4) biuret test positive.

benzyl alcohol+1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzeneP: ether
nitrobenzene(i) Sn/HCl (ii) NaNO₂/HCl <5 °C (iii) 2-naphthol/OH⁻Q: azo dye
n-glucoseH⁺, polymerisationR: starch  S: amino acids → polymer (protein)
  1. P → 3; Q → 2,3; R → 1; S → 4
  2. P → 2; Q → 2,3; R → 1; S → 3,4
  3. P → 3; Q → 2,3; R → 1; S → 3,4
  4. P → 3; Q → 2; R → 4; S → 1,3
Answer and solution

Answer: (3)

The nitro ether contains N (3). The azo-naphthol contains a phenolic OH and N (2, 3). Starch is a carbohydrate (1). A protein contains N and peptide bonds (3, 4).

Q138Single correct option

D-Glyceraldehyde + HCN/Ba(CN)₂ gives two cyanohydrins X and Y; SnCl₂/HCl then H₂O converts X to Z and Y to W; HNO₃ oxidises Z to an optically inactive acid V. Match: X, Y, W, Z with (1) threo cyanohydrin; (2) D-erythrose; (3) D-threose; (4) erythro cyanohydrin.

D-glyceraldehydeHCN, Ba(CN)₂X (erythro cyanohydrin)+Y (threo cyanohydrin)
Z: D-erythroseHNO₃V: meso-tartaric acid | W: D-threose
  1. X → 1; Y → 2; W → 3; Z → 4
  2. X → 4; Y → 1; W → 3; Z → 2
  3. X → 1; Y → 3; W → 2; Z → 4
  4. X → 4; Y → 3; W → 2; Z → 1
Answer and solution

Answer: (2): X → 4, Y → 1, W → 3, Z → 2

The Kiliani–Fischer extension gives erythro and threo cyanohydrins. Z oxidised to an optically inactive (meso) tartaric acid must be D-erythrose, which comes from the erythro cyanohydrin X; the threo cyanohydrin Y gives D-threose, W.

Q139One or more options correct

D-Glucose is converted: (i) red P/HI; (ii) Al₂O₃, Cr₂O₃, heat; (iii) conc. H₂SO₄ + HNO₃ to A (nitrobenzene); then Sn/HCl and NaNO₂/HCl (0–5 °C) give B (diazonium salt); (i) CuCN/heat, (ii) SnCl₂ + HCl, (iii) H₂O gives C (benzaldehyde); C reacts with HCHO/OH⁻ (1 equivalent) to give D (aromatic) and E. Select the correct statements:

D-glucose(i) red P/HI; (ii) Al₂O₃, Cr₂O₃/Δ; (iii) HNO₃/H₂SO₄A: nitrobenzene(i) Sn/HCl (ii) NaNO₂/HCl, 0–5 °CB: diazonium salt
(i) CuCN/Δ (ii) SnCl₂/HCl (iii) H₂OC: benzaldehydeHCHO, OH⁻ (1 eq.)D: benzyl alcohol+E: HCOO⁻
  1. C shows disproportionation (Cannizzaro) with conc. NaOH
  2. C forms a diazonium salt with HNO₂
  3. C gives a foul-smelling compound with CHCl₃ + KOH
  4. C is a primary amine
  5. B on H₃O⁺/Δ, then Na, then CH₃Cl gives anisole
  6. D is PhCH₂N=CH₂
  7. E is sodium benzoate
Answer and solution

Answer: (1) and (5)

C is benzaldehyde, which has no α-hydrogen and undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction. B → phenol → sodium phenoxide → anisole. D is benzyl alcohol and E is sodium formate (crossed Cannizzaro).

Q140One or more options correct

For the complex dichloridobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) sulphate:

  1. its formula is [Co(en)₂Cl₂]SO₄
  2. the coordination number of Co is 6
  3. the effective atomic number of Co is 32
  4. it is a heteroleptic complex
Answer and solution

Answer: (2) and (4)

The cation is [Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ so the salt is [Co(en)₂Cl₂]₂SO₄. EAN = 27 − 3 + 12 = 36. It has two different ligand types, so it is heteroleptic.

Li, Mg and Be form nitrides.
